title: sessions listing shows 0 messages, no timestamps and no titles: claude_code discover() never reads transcripts
description:
**Observed on real data (read-only run against `--home` default, origin/develop `9fc6584`):** `botspy sessions` prints `MSGS 0`, `LAST ACTIVITY —`, `TITLE —` and empty `metadata` for **every** claude_code row; `-o json` shows `started_at`: "", `last_activity_at`: "", `message_count`: 0, `metadata`: {} for all 43 listed sessions. The same sessions open fine: `botspy show synth-1a2b0003` reports "3 messages, started 2026-08-14T10:41:27.032Z".

**Repro:**
1. `cargo build --release` at origin/develop; run `./target/release/botspy sessions --limit 5` (real home) → every row `0  —  —`.
2. `./target/release/botspy sessions --limit 5 -o json` → all `message_count` 0, timestamps empty.
3. `./target/release/botspy show synth-1a2b0003` → same session shows 3 messages with timestamps. Inconsistent.

**Expected:** the listing carries real per-session data — message count, first/last activity timestamps, and title — consistent with `botspy show` for the same id, without writing anything to the source.

**Suspected code:** `ClaudeCodeSource::discover()` in `src/adapters/claude_code.rs` (~line 81-106): it pushes `SessionSummary { id, agent, project_id, ..SessionSummary::default() }` per `.jsonl` file name and never reads the transcript. `extract()` in the same file already parses everything correctly.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `discover()` populates `started_at`, `last_activity_at`, `message_count` and title metadata per transcript, matching what `open()`/`show` reports for the same id.
- Regression test with a **synthetic fixture** (temp-dir transcript or the committed `tests/fixtures` corpus — never real transcripts): a transcript with N timestamped records must list `message_count: N` and the correct first/last timestamps in `discover()` output.
- `botspy sessions` and `botspy show` agree on message counts and timestamps for the fixture sessions.
- Read-only guarantee unchanged: no writes into the source tree.
- Note: `botspy sources`, `botspy doctor` and `botspy show` already work correctly on real data; only the listing path is broken.
- Related: the local-store ingestion epic BOTSPY-6f173d builds on `Adapter::discover()` (task BOTSPY-a48fb1) — populated summaries benefit it, and it changes no adapter code, so no conflict.

comments.author: example-user
comments.text: Fixed on develop (commit bc4caa7, branch fix/sessions-listing-bugs-a). ClaudeCodeSource::discover() now scans each transcript through a throwaway extractor — side-effect free, does not consume resume offsets — and summaries carry message_count, started_at/last_activity_at and the recorded title, consistent with show. Spec-first: two scenarios added to features/cli/20_sessions.feature (Summaries carry real activity; Human output shows the recorded session title), watched fail (0 msgs / — title), then made green; regression unit test discovery_summaries_carry_activity_from_the_transcripts uses a synthetic temp-dir transcript. Full suite green: cargo test, cargo test --test bdd (162 passed), clippy -D warnings, doc -D warnings, fmt. Verified read-only: no writes to the source tree. Note for follow-up: cursor/codex/grok_bot/antigravity discover() share the same default-summary defect; left to their adapter epics (BOTSPY-4661a5, BOTSPY-357602, BOTSPY-5a3bed, BOTSPY-55ea2f).

comments.author: example-user
comments.text: Follow-up (commit e221521 on develop): the regression test added here reused the botspy-cc3-{pid} temp root that malformed_and_unknown_are_skipped_and_counted also uses; the two run as parallel threads and one test's remove_dir_all could wipe the other's transcript — the flaky musl x86_64 CI failures seen on runs 37072051132 and 37072294147 (summaries.len() 0 vs 1). The test now has a unique root tag (botspy-cc5). No behavior change; status stays closed.
